episodes.156673: After morning thunderstorms shifted southeast of the area, a second large complex of thunderstorms redeveloped over Mississippi during the late morning and early afternoon hours.  This complex shifted east into Alabama during the mid to late afternoon hours, exiting northeast Alabama during the early evening hours.  Several reports of thunderstorm wind damage were received, along with one large hail report.  In addition, rainfall of 1-2 inches fell in a very short period of time, causing flash flooding that washed out a bridge in Cullman County and flooded several streets in Marshall County.

episodes.157012: Numerous thunderstorms developed over the mainland and moved across the Brevard County intracoastal and nearshore coastal waters during the evening. A few of the storms produced strong/severe wind gusts near the coast before the storms moved to the Atlantic.
episodes.157015: Several thunderstorms moved from the mainland, across north Merritt Island, to the Atlantic during the early evening. One of the thunderstorms briefly became severe and produced winds over 50 knots at the Kennedy Space Center.
episodes.157200: A line of strong storms brought measured wind gusts in excess of 34 knots to portions of the Gulf county and Franklin county coasts.
episodes.157202: A squall line pushed through the region, bringing widespread impacts to trees and power lines, particularly across portions of southeast Alabama and southwest Georgia.  Measured wind gusts of 60-70 mph occurred in southwest Georgia.

episodes.157265: Early on May 3rd, central Kentucky sat in the warm sector ahead of an approaching surface low. Much of the region saw only rain showers, but one isolated cell in southern Kentucky was able to produce a short lived EF-1 tornado in the city of Tompkinsville, KY. ||On May 4th, a cold front, following the first system, produced additional rain showers and thunderstorms on the already saturated ground. The result was widespread flash flooding with isolated severe wind damage.
episodes.157419: A swift moving cold front brought a brief bout of strong storms to south central Nebraska during the afternoon hours on May 5th. Thunderstorms developed along the cold front from SW to NE, generally along a line from Franklin County to Nance County around 3pm, and moved SE. Most of this activity was fairly weak and poorly organized. However, shortly before 4pm CDT, a stronger storm developed over Clay County and managed to produce nickel size hail and a brief landspout tornado. This became the second event in only a few days where landspout tornadoes were reported in this general area of south central Nebraska. No damage or impacts from the landspout were reported, so it was given an EFU rating. The line of thunderstorms continued SE with no additional severe reports, and exited the area around 6pm CDT.
episodes.157420: A swift moving cold front brought a brief bout of severe storms to north central Kansas during the afternoon hours on May 5th. Thunderstorms developed along the cold front from SW to NE, generally along a line from Stockton to Smith Center around 3pm, and moved SE. Most of this activity was fairly weak and poorly organized. However, shortly before 4pm CDT, a stronger storm developed along the state line in far NE Smith County and managed to produce a small swath of severe hail from far NE Smith County into far W Mitchell County. The largest hail reported from this storm was 2 inches in diameter, though it is believed that the majority of hail was in the 1-1.5 inch range. The line of thunderstorms continued SE with no additional severe reports, and exited the area around 6pm CDT.
episodes.157484: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front producing two tornadoes and hail and wind reports.
episodes.157572: With weakening trade winds over the Aloha State and a trough to the northwest, heavy showers formed over leeward sections of the Big Island and East Maui.  The rain produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  There were no reports of significant property damage or injuries.
episodes.157613: A retrograding upper level ridge and stronger, moist SW steering flow primed an unstable airmass across SE GA during the late evening hours where a few severe strong developed along a leading pre-frontal trough axis aided by a passing mid level short wave trough aloft.
episodes.157833: A nearly stationary corridor of thunderstorms developed from central Kentucky to northwest Tennessee, including Christian and Todd Counties. These storms resulted in excessive rainfall amounts over places that received heavy rain during the early morning severe storms. The storms occurred in a narrow axis of instability along a southeastward moving cold front.
episodes.158441: A multi-day severe weather event unfolded across Central Alabama from May 2nd through May 4th.  Alabama remained on the eastern side of a broad upper trough positioned over the Plains States. Several upper level impulses emanated from the trough axis and produced severe weather across Alabama. The main severe weather event occurred on May 4th when a QLCS tracked eastward across areas along and east of I-20 and produced widespread wind damage, flash flooding, and tornadoes.
episodes.158541: A potent spring storm system swept across the southeast during the day. An associated strong cold front moved with numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developing across the area, resulting in widespread wind damage and very heavy rain.
episodes.158815: A warm front lifted north into Pennsylvania during the day and became stalled during the early evening across the northeastern part of the Commonwealth. Thunderstorms became aligned along the Wyoming Valley, and extended off to the east into the Lackawaxen Valley during the evening. Rainfall amounts between 2 to 3 inches fell in a very short amount of time over urban and moderately populated rural areas leading to several road closures, overtopped bridges and small stream flash flooding.
episodes.158886: In the early morning hours on May 5th 2021, a cold front and associated band of showers and storms pushed across portions of southeastern Louisiana. This cluster of storms would eventually slow down as the cold front stalled across the northern Gulf leading to flash flooding across a few locations of southeastern Louisiana.
episodes.158910: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rain in portions of southwest Alabama.
episodes.158970: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.158972: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.158997: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.159019: Heavy rain brought flooding to several rivers in early May. It was all about the rain in May. High moisture levels yielded heavy downpours and wet conditions from western into central Arkansas. Showers were not as appreciable along the Mississippi River due to a ridge of high pressure to the east.
episodes.159022: Isolated severe thunderstorm in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of the Lower Maryland Eastern Shore.
episodes.159023: Isolated thunderstorm in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Maryland Coastal Waters.
episodes.159172: A series of upper-level short waves moved across the region in persistent, southwesterly upper-level flow combined with moderate instability and shear to produce several rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms across north and central Georgia. Some of these storms dumped 2 to 4 inches of rain over the area, resulting in isolated flash flooding.
episodes.159287: A cold front pushed through the CWA with decent instability ahead and along it with values around 1000-1500 J/Kg. Wind shear was on the weaker side of around 20kts but enough updraft forcing to produce up to quarter sized hail and around 60 mph wind gusts for Dodge City to Tice and points to the southeast.
